Load development version of the Julia package UniversalDiffEq.jl and check version number

```{r}
JuliaCall::julia_setup()
JuliaCall::julia_eval('using Pkg; Pkg.add(url = "https://github.com/Jack-H-Buckner/UniversalDiffEq.jl.git")')

JuliaCall::julia_eval("using UniversalDiffEq; string(pkgversion(UniversalDiffEq))")
```


Load packages and setup emude

```{r}
library(devtools)
library(JuliaCall)
library(tidyverse)
library(emude)
emude_setup()
```

Create 3 datasets:

- one time series simulated from a logistic growth model with carrying capacity $K$
- one time series simulated from a Ricker model with carrying capacity $2K$
- multiple time series simulated from both models

```{r}
#Initial population size and parameters
N0 <- 10 #initial population size
tsteps <- 150 #time steps
r <- 0.05 #growth rate
K <- 100

#Ricker model
Ricker <- data.frame(t = 1:tsteps, N_t = NA_real_)
Ricker$N_t[1] <- N0

for(t in 1:(tsteps-1)){
  Ricker$N_t[t+1] <- Ricker$N_t[t]*exp(r*(1 - Ricker$N_t[t]/K))
}

#Logistic growth model
Logistic <- data.frame(t = 1:tsteps, N_t = NA_real_, dNdt = NA_real_)
Logistic$N_t[1] <- N0

for(t in 1:(tsteps-1)){
  Logistic$dNdt[t] <- r*Logistic$N_t[t]*(1 - Logistic$N_t[t]/(2*K))
  Logistic$N_t[t+1] <- Logistic$N_t[t] + Logistic$dNdt[t]
}

discrete_pop <- Ricker
continuous_pop <- Logistic[,1:2]
both_pops <- bind_rows(Ricker, Logistic[,1:2], .id = "series")

ggplot() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = K, color = "black") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 2*K, color = "yellow4") +
  geom_point(data = Logistic, aes(x = t, y = N_t), color = "yellow4") +
  geom_point(data = Ricker, aes(x = t, y = N_t)) +
  labs(x="Time",
       y="Population size (individuals)") +
  theme_classic()
```

# Discrete-time model constructors

## Non-parameteric models

### Test for NNDE()

Split data into training and testing sets, construct model, train model, predict on testing data, and construct a series plot
```{r}
discrete_pop_split <- 
  split_series(data = discrete_pop, time_column_name = "t", train_frac = 0.49)

discrete_pop_train <- discrete_pop_split$train
discrete_pop_test <- discrete_pop_split$test

diff_model <- 
  NNDE(data = discrete_pop_train,
       time_column_name = "t")

train_UDE(diff_model, loss_function = "joint likelihood")

diff_preds <- 
  predict_UDE(diff_model, test_data = discrete_pop_test)

series_plot(observations = discrete_pop, x = t, y = N_t, 
            predictions = diff_preds)
```

### Test for multi_NNDE()

Split data into training and testing sets, construct model, train model, predict on testing data, and construct a series plot
```{r}
both_pops_split <- 
  split_series(data = both_pops, time_column_name = "t",
               series_column_name = "series", train_frac = 0.49)

both_pops_train <- both_pops_split$train
both_pops_test <- both_pops_split$test

multi_diff_model <-
  multi_NNDE(data = both_pops_train,
             time_column_name = "t",
             series_column_name = "series")

train_UDE(multi_diff_model, loss_function = "joint likelihood")

multi_diff_preds <-
  predict_UDE(multi_diff_model, test_data = both_pops_test)

series_plot(observations = both_pops, x = t, y = N_t, group = series,
            predictions = multi_diff_preds)
```

## Parametric models

Create the Ricker model function

```{r}
ricker <- function(u,nn,p,t){
  stepu = u[1]*exp(nn[1]*(1-u[1]/p$K[1])) 
  return(c(stepu))
}

multi_ricker <- function(u,i,nn,p,t){
  stepu = u[1]*exp(nn[1]*(1-u[1]/p$K[i])) 
  return(c(stepu))
}
```

### Test for custom_difference()

Split data into training and testing sets, construct model, train model, predict on testing data, and construct a series plot
```{r}
discrete_pop_split <- 
  split_series(data = discrete_pop, time_column_name = "t", train_frac = 0.49)

discrete_pop_train <- discrete_pop_split$train
discrete_pop_test <- discrete_pop_split$test

diff_model <- 
  custom_difference(data = discrete_pop_train, step = ricker, 
                    initial_parameters = list(K = K),
                    time_column_name = "t")

train_UDE(diff_model, loss_function = "joint likelihood")

diff_preds <- 
  predict_UDE(diff_model, test_data = discrete_pop_test)

series_plot(observations = discrete_pop, x = t, y = N_t, 
            predictions = diff_preds)
```

### Test for multi_custom_difference()

Split data into training and testing sets, construct model, train model, predict on testing data, and construct a series plot
```{r}
both_pops_split <- 
  split_series(data = both_pops, time_column_name = "t",
               series_column_name = "series", train_frac = 0.49)

both_pops_train <- both_pops_split$train
both_pops_test <- both_pops_split$test

multi_diff_model <-
  multi_custom_difference(data = both_pops_train, step = multi_ricker,
                          initial_parameters = list(K = c(K,2*K)),
                          time_column_name = "t",
                          series_column_name = "series")

train_UDE(multi_diff_model, loss_function = "joint likelihood")

multi_diff_preds <-
  predict_UDE(multi_diff_model, test_data = both_pops_test)

series_plot(observations = both_pops, x = t, y = N_t, group = series,
            predictions = multi_diff_preds)
```


# Continuous-time model constructors

## Non-parametric models

### Test for NODE()

Split data into training and testing sets, construct model, train model, predict on testing data, and construct a series plot
```{r}
continuous_pop_split <- 
  split_series(data = continuous_pop, time_column_name = "t", train_frac = 0.49)

continuous_pop_train <- continuous_pop_split$train
continuous_pop_test <- continuous_pop_split$test

deriv_model <- 
  NODE(data = continuous_pop_train, 
       time_column_name = "t")

train_UDE(deriv_model, loss_function = "derivative matching")

deriv_preds <- 
  predict_UDE(deriv_model, test_data = continuous_pop_test)

series_plot(observations = continuous_pop, x = t, y = N_t, 
            predictions = deriv_preds)
```

### Test for multi_NODE()

Split data into training and testing sets, construct model, train model, predict on testing data, and construct a series plot
```{r}
both_pops_split <- 
  split_series(data = both_pops, time_column_name = "t",
               series_column_name = "series", train_frac = 0.49)

both_pops_train <- both_pops_split$train
both_pops_test <- both_pops_split$test

multi_deriv_model <- 
  multi_NODE(data = both_pops_train, 
             time_column_name = "t",
             series_column_name = "series")

train_UDE(multi_deriv_model, loss_function = "derivative matching")

multi_deriv_preds <- 
  predict_UDE(multi_deriv_model, test_data = both_pops_test)

series_plot(observations = both_pops, x = t, y = N_t, group = series,
            predictions = multi_deriv_preds)
```

## Parametric models

Create the logistic growth model function
```{r}
logistic <- function(u,nn,p,t){
  dudt = u[1]*nn[1]*(1-u[1]/p$K[1])
  return(c(dudt))
}

multi_logistic <- function(u,i,nn,p,t){
  dudt = u[1]*nn[1]*(1-u[1]/p$K[i])
  return(c(dudt))
}
```

### Test for custom_derivatives()

Split data into training and testing sets, construct model, train model, predict on testing data, and construct a series plot
```{r}
continuous_pop_split <- 
  split_series(data = continuous_pop, time_column_name = "t", train_frac = 0.49)

continuous_pop_train <- continuous_pop_split$train
continuous_pop_test <- continuous_pop_split$test

deriv_model <- 
  custom_derivatives(data = continuous_pop_train, derivs = logistic, 
                     initial_parameters = list(K = 2*K),
                     time_column_name = "t")

train_UDE(deriv_model, loss_function = "derivative matching")

deriv_preds <- 
  predict_UDE(deriv_model, test_data = continuous_pop_test)

series_plot(observations = continuous_pop, x = t, y = N_t, 
            predictions = deriv_preds)
```

### Test for multi_custom_derivatives()

Split data into training and testing sets, construct model, train model, predict on testing data, and construct a series plot
```{r}
both_pops_split <- 
  split_series(data = both_pops, time_column_name = "t",
               series_column_name = "series", train_frac = 0.49)

both_pops_train <- both_pops_split$train
both_pops_test <- both_pops_split$test

multi_deriv_model <- 
  multi_custom_derivatives(data = both_pops_train, derivs = multi_logistic, 
                           initial_parameters = list(K = c(K,2*K)),
                           time_column_name = "t",
                           series_column_name = "series")

train_UDE(multi_deriv_model, loss_function = "derivative matching")

multi_deriv_preds <- 
  predict_UDE(multi_deriv_model, test_data = both_pops_test)

series_plot(observations = both_pops, x = t, y = N_t, group = series,
            predictions = multi_deriv_preds)
```
